chapter: Records, Lovie Austin and a first marriage
title: Paramount payments, Mayo Williams and Mr. Supper, royalties
summary: M. A. Supper paid honestly while J. Mayo Williams was a thief; she got $75 a side and a quarter-cent royalty, and only got her copyright back from Mills.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Tell me about Paramount and getting paid.
Well now, I tell you about Paramount. Paramount -- Mr. Ink Williams, a fellow named J. Mayo Williams --
Mayo, sure.

He was the -- I think he's the one that first came into Dreamland and spoke to me about recording. But Mr. Supper, Mr. M. A. Supper, the white fellow -- J. Mayo Williams was a colored man, Negro man. Mr. Supper was a white man and a very fine, honest man.
Of course, Mayo Williams (inaudible).
Mayo Williams was a thief.
I know. I met him.
He was the one.
Right.

Now, Mr. Supper always paid me my money. When he'd promise me, if it was $10.00, he gave me $10.00. Whatever he promised me, he gave to me, and I remember once Mr. Supper, if I'm not mistaken, gave me $368.00 in one check, if I'm not mistaken.

But in the meantime Mayo Williams had gotten with Mr. -- not with Mr. Supper -- but I think he had gone to Mills and them -- Mills Music -- and I don't know what he did, but I think he maneuvered a little bit and got some of my money. See?
Yes, that was his way.

That was his way. But Mr. Supper was an honest man. He never cheated me out of a dime. And -- but the contract, you see, the contracts, you got $75.00 a side. And your contract was a fourth of a penny -- I think I've got some -- royalties.
Now, that was on your own -- on your compositions or anything you did?
On -- on my compositions, on the records and everything. It all included -- it was inclusive.
I see.
See, the records and the song and all, that fourth of a penny. For instance, if a record sold, whether it was my song on it or not, I only got a fourth of a penny. See?
Uh-huh. So you were getting, actually getting royalties. Did you get it?

Well, I got $368.00, I remember very well. That's the only thing I ever remember getting, from all that money they made, until I finally went to Mills, and the copyright came due, and I beat them to the punch. I got my copyright. See? Then I started getting a little money, and I don't get anything like I should get and never have gotten anything like I should have gotten. You understand? Never. I've never gotten -- and right now today they're still making money.
And you see they got these skeleton -- what do you call it, recordings, people out stealing your songs, and I'm not getting a dime. You see?
